svg.title: How much of their own engineering do AI models do? Google DeepMind versus Anthropic self-reports
svg.desc: Horizontal bars, 0 to 100 percent. Google DeepMind, from the Gemini 4 Argon Safety and Security Report as covered on October 14 to 16, 2026: more than 75 percent of production code is AI-written; about 88 percent of pull requests still need multi-turn human steering or human-written code; fully delegated pull requests rose from 7.5 percent in April 2026 to 11.9 percent in September 2026; Gemini 4 Argon solved about half of 74 RE-Bench machine-learning engineering tasks. Anthropic, from its October 16 reports: staff median estimate that AI already does 51 percent of the work of building a frontier model; about 80 percent of interactive agent session time is spent waiting on a human. Footnote: different metrics and methods, self-reported, not directly comparable. DeepMind concludes the risk from AI-driven ML R and D is currently low.
svg.text: AI doing AI-lab work: two labs' self-reports (Oct 14–16)
Google DeepMind (Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report)
Pull requests still needing human steering or human code
Pull requests fully delegated to AI (April → September 2026)
RE-Bench ML-engineering tasks solved by Argon (74 tasks)
Staff median estimate: share of frontier-model work AI does today
Interactive agent-session time spent waiting on a human
Different metrics, methods and definitions. All figures are self-reported by each lab; none is independently reproduced.
DeepMind: "no significant" end-to-end acceleration of ML R&D; risk "currently low". A LessWrong critique says ~¼ of
scored RE-Bench tasks were unpassable. Anthropic: agents logged 6× their handlers' hours by August.
